findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so one code can be used twice
findings.body:
`authorize` reads `user.backupCodes` at the start of the request, decrypts it, nulls the matched entry and writes the whole blob back. There is no transaction, no optimistic check that the stored ciphertext is unchanged, and no row lock.

Two concurrent sign-ins with the same backup code both see it as valid and both succeed, which breaks the 'usable exactly once' guarantee. Two concurrent sign-ins with different codes can also overwrite each other's update, so one consumed code comes back to life.

Fix: wrap the read and write in a transaction with a conditional update, e.g. `updateMany where { id, backupCodes: <old ciphertext> }` and fail the login if 0 rows are affected.

findings.title: Backup code match is case- and whitespace-sensitive while the UI hints uppercase
findings.body:
Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`). The input only has dashes stripped before an exact `indexOf` match.

The BackupCode input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which invites uppercase entry. Uppercase input, or a pasted code with surrounding whitespace or a newline, is rejected as `IncorrectBackupCode`.

The same exact-match logic is in `disable.ts` (line 61). Normalize with `.trim().toLowerCase()` in both places.

findings.title: 2FA is already enabled when the backup-codes step shows, but `onEnable` only runs from the Close button
findings.body:
After a successful `/totp/enable`, the modal now moves to `DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()`. `onEnable()` and `resetState()` are only invoked by the 'Close' button.

If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (Escape, overlay click, i.e. through `onOpenChange`), the parent never learns that 2FA was enabled. The settings switch keeps showing 2FA as disabled even though it is active server-side. The modal also stays stuck on the backup-codes step for the next open.

Fix: call `onEnable` as soon as the enable succeeds (and only defer closing), or handle dismissal in `onOpenChange` while on that step.

findings.title: `missing_backup_codes` message points to a regeneration feature that does not exist
findings.body:
Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null` and get "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings."

There is no UI to generate or regenerate backup codes. The only path is to disable 2FA (which needs a working TOTP code) and enable it again. The message should describe that path, or a regeneration feature should be added.

findings.title: Non-string `backupCode` in the request body causes an unhandled 500
findings.body:
`req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` is called on any truthy value. A JSON body with a numeric or object `backupCode` throws a TypeError and produces a 500 instead of a 400.

The endpoint also throws raw `Error`s instead of returning JSON for the missing-key case, which the client maps to a generic error. Validate the body type before use.
